ListBrowsingPositionTests.Alphabet_secti.reason: The original Elan with acute accent, leading-space Zelda, 123 Robots and trademark fixtures are exact cases, with decomposed accents, non-Latin letters, empty titles and multi-character uppercase expansion covered too.

tests.case: spine preserves ordering and selection with source pointer, scrub, halo and keyboard behavior
scrubs an unavailable M to P and resolves an equal distance toward the earlier stop
interpolates the viewport halo in the displayed order and returns the wave to rest

ListBrowsingPositionTests.Alphabet_spine.reason: Both native desktop views use the source eight titles and a constrained scroll viewport. Assertions cover 27 notches, half-way proportional drag, transparent rail, fixed 27 letters, unavailable stops, 24px targets, 11px ink, right-edge alignment beside the separate scrollbar, reserved artwork space, hover without scrolling, fractional four-row wave with no reduced-motion transition, pointer halo on unavailable M with the same scroll as keyboard P, unchanged selection/order, descending C activation, viewport halo and wave reset on leave. The obsolete method name mentions switching sort; its source assertions actually preserve each active name-sort direction, as these tests do.

ListBrowsingPositionTests.Adding_to_a_li.reason: Grid and list native tests scroll the source eight-title fixture to 200, select its last alphabetical title without scrolling, add it to an existing list, compare the exact offset and verify the saved release membership through the production API.

ListBrowsingPositionTests.Closing_detail.reason: Both native desktop views open Details at offset 200, deliberately change the retained Library to zero underneath it, close Details and assert restoration to the exact original offset. Fullscreen retains its independent paged presentation, with a separate assertion that it does not acquire the desktop spine.
